key_facts: The UK state pension 'triple lock' raises benefits by the greatest of 2.5%, earnings growth, or inflation; benefits have risen far faster than workers' earnings since its introduction in 2011, and funding it has cost the state billions more than initially envisaged. The state pension is set to top £150bn a year, the single most expensive benefit.

According to the OECD, UK retirement benefits (after tax, including automatic enrolment in occupational schemes) equal 54.2% of average UK earnings, versus an average of 63.2% across wealthy countries; including income from other occupational and personal pensions narrows the gap. The OECD's most recent UK gender pension gap figure is for 2021, showing women's pensions about a third lower than men's, versus a typical ~22.8% gap in wealthy countries.

Andy Burnham intends to replace the triple lock with a system raising the state pension by at least inflation or 2.5%, removing the automatic link with average earnings; this would likely mean less generous increases, though it would track earnings growth over the longer term. Pensioner relative poverty (below 60% of typical household income) has risen slightly over the last decade after housing costs, though it remains lower than for families with children or working-age people.
importance_reason: Policy debate on pension indexation with a long-horizon fiscal impact, but no immediate market-moving event or decision.
market_link: Changes to triple-lock indexation affect UK public spending and borrowing outlook, which can influence gilt yields over the long term; effect is indirect.

key_facts: The UK government will commit £100m to establish a national AI Biosecurity Lab (AIBL), described as a 'world first' institute, with support from leading AI firms, as part of Wednesday's Budget.

The Chancellor will also commit an additional £120m to the UK's AI Security Institute (AISI), £60m to a 'National Cyber Shield' using agentic AI for cyber-defence, and £70m to a National Exposure and Real-Time Vulnerability (NERV) Centre.
OpenAI and Anthropic will provide £200m worth of AI model credits to be used for their models in support of the AIBL.
Full details of the role and remit of the AIBL have not yet been published; the AI Minister described it as a 'major new global institution'.
importance_reason: Крупный публичный бюджетный пакет в области AI-безопасности и биобезопасности, но без детализации мандата и без прямого рыночного эффекта.
